name: Nanubae, Wambrumas variety
confidence_why: no confirmed first-hand statement: the record's source was not confirmed

catalog_locator: sec. 2.3.2.2 'Stress', printed p. 17 = PDF p. 22 of 60; file the copy we hold (-f 22 -l 22)
catalog_quote: Stress was only marked on Wambrumas list, and even there, MacKenzie did not indicate stress on every word. As a result, only tentative conclusions about stress can be drawn. It appears that stress was generally on the ultimate syllable. If there is a suffix or it is a compound word, the last syllable of the stem is stressed and there may be secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tentatively, primary stress falls on the word-final syllable; in suffixed words and compounds it falls on the final syllable of the (first) stem, i.e. stem-final rather than strictly word-final.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Possible secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme in suffixed/compound words.
new_statements.exceptions: None beyond the suffix/compound behaviour; authors stress that the conclusions are tentative because stress was marked on only one wordlist (Wambrumas) and not on every word.
new_statements.domain_note: Based on impressionistic stress marks on a 170/190-item SIL survey wordlist elicited in Wambrumas village in Feb 2005 (citation forms); word-level, no phrase-level discussion. Sociolinguistic survey report, not a phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement rests solely on the wordlist elicited in Wambrumas (Wamblamas) village, i.e. the Nanubae proper / Wambrumas-Yamandim dialect (Glottolog wamb1260 under Nanbay nanb1234, within nanu1240). Nothing is said about stress in the Imanmeri (iman1240, 'Imangae'/Aunda/Tuaimunda) variety, whose lexical similarity to Wambrumas is low enough that the survey questions whether it is the same language. Older literature calls the language Alfendio / Arafundi / Arafuni (Dye's list 'at Wablamas').

sources.note: Sec. 2.3.2.2 'Stress', p. 17 (PDF p. 22): stress was marked only on the Wambrumas (= Wamblamas village, Nanubae) wordlist and not on every word; tentatively 'generally on the ultimate syllable'; with a suffix or in a compound the last syllable of the stem is stressed, with possible secondary stress on the last syllable of the second morpheme. Appendix D wordlists (pp. 48ff) are printed without stress marks.
